zy55gr:245: Unlike DeepSeek-V3's 256 64-dimensional experts (each token selects top-k), K2.5 clusters token representations into 384 clusters, each corresponding to an expert sub-network. Routing is essentially a nearest-neighbor query from token to cluster. Potential advantages of this design: expert boundaries are determined by the data distribution and do not need manual setup; experts are more mutually exclusive (tokens in the same cluster do not have routing conflicts). Potential risk: clustering quality determines the upper bound of expert specialization, and tokens in niche domains may be misclassified.
